# Exact convex feasibility of ray endpoints and planar sector areas

## 1. Data and theorem

Fix cyclically ordered nonzero points P_1,...,P_m, one on each of m rays from 0, with every consecutive angular gap strictly less than pi. The rays cover the full circle. Indices are cyclic. Prescribe a finite nonnegative area A_i for the closed sector cone(P_i,P_(i+1)). Put

    D_i=det(P_i,P_(i+1))>0,
    t_i=2A_i/D_i,
    a_i=t_i-1,
    E_i=det(P_(i-1),P_(i+1)),
    kappa_i=D_(i-1)+D_i-E_i.                       (1)

In this note E_i denotes a determinant, not a sector envelope area.

**Theorem.** These data are realized by a planar convex body K with 0 in its interior, boundary(K) intersect the i-th ray equal to P_i, and the prescribed sector areas, if and only if both conditions hold:

* t_i>=1 for every i;
* there are u_i,v_i>0 with u_i+v_i=t_i such that

    D_i a_(i-1)/u_(i-1)+D_(i-1) a_i/v_i<=kappa_i
                                                        (2)

for every i.

When feasible, the data have a polygonal realization with at most one new vertex in each sector:

    V_i=u_i P_i+v_i P_(i+1),
    K=union_i conv{0,P_i,V_i,P_(i+1)}.             (3)

For six rays from three lines, this is an exact finite description of all jointly realizable central endpoints and sector areas, with at most 12 vertices. It is not a collection of independent sector bounds: consecutive sectors share the constraints (2).

Eliminating v_i=t_i-u_i makes (2) a convex system on the open intervals 0<u_i<t_i. Section 4 gives an equivalent compact closed domain, including zero area excesses. Thus existence is an attained finite feasibility question, not a limit of putative bodies.

## 2. Necessity

Every actual body with the given endpoints contains each core triangle conv{0,P_i,P_(i+1)}, of area D_i/2. Therefore t_i>=1.

The theorem proved in `candidate be9098c627b40217` supplies an exact polygonal replacement with those same endpoints and sector areas and at most one new vertex per sector. Its new vertex has the form V_i=u_i P_i+v_i P_(i+1), with u_i,v_i>0 and

    u_i+v_i=2A_i/D_i=t_i.

When the sector is just its core triangle, any interior point of its outer chord can serve as a redundant V_i; take u_i=v_i=1/2.

Convexity at the prescribed endpoint P_i requires

    det(P_i-V_(i-1),V_i-P_i)>=0.                  (4)

Expanding gives exactly

    u_(i-1)(1-u_i)D_(i-1)
    +v_i(1-v_(i-1))D_i
    -u_(i-1)v_i E_i>=0.

Divide by the positive u_(i-1)v_i and use

    (1-u_i)/v_i=1-a_i/v_i,
    (1-v_(i-1))/u_(i-1)=1-a_(i-1)/u_(i-1).

The result is (2). Thus the finite constraints are necessary for every actual convex body, not just for an initially polygonal one.

## 3. Sufficiency and the exact joining inequality

Suppose t_i>=1 and positive u_i,v_i satisfy (2). Each piece in (3) is convex, has the two prescribed ray endpoints, and has area

    (u_i+v_i)D_i/2=A_i.

For completeness we prove that the entire union is convex. This does not follow merely from each piece being convex.

In sector coordinates w=x P_i+y P_(i+1), x,y>=0, define

    p_i=(1-u_i)/v_i=1-a_i/v_i,
    q_i=(1-v_i)/u_i=1-a_i/u_i,
    f_i(w)=max{x+p_i y,q_i x+y}.                  (5)

If t_i=1, then p_i=q_i=1 and the sector piece is the core triangle. If t_i>1, p_i,q_i<1 and 1-p_i q_i=(t_i-1)/(u_i v_i)>0. Direct intersection of the two displayed halfplanes shows that the unit sublevel of f_i in the sector is precisely conv{0,P_i,V_i,P_(i+1)}. In either case f_i is positive away from 0, convex on the sector, and positively homogeneous. At both bounding rays it equals the radial parameter, so the sector definitions glue to a continuous function f on the plane, with f(0)=0.

We compute its slope jump at the shared ray through P_i. Use coordinates w=x P_i+y P_(i+1) in a neighborhood of a nonzero point on that ray. The adjacent endpoint has coordinates

    P_(i-1)=(E_i/D_i)P_i-(D_(i-1)/D_i)P_(i+1).

On the left side y<0, the edge ending at P_i gives the local gauge

    x+[(E_i-D_i q_(i-1))/D_(i-1)]y.

On the right side y>0, the edge starting at P_i gives the local gauge

    x+p_i y.

These descriptions remain valid when a neighboring sector has zero excess: its two gauge forms then coincide. When its excess is positive, the other form is strictly less at the shared ray, so the displayed form is indeed active locally.

The right slope minus the left slope in the transverse coordinate y is

    [D_(i-1)p_i+D_i q_(i-1)-E_i]/D_(i-1),

which is nonnegative exactly when (2) holds. Thus there is no downward slope jump at any shared ray. Along every affine line avoiding 0, the restriction of f is continuous and piecewise linear, convex within each sector, and has no downward slope jump at sector crossings. It is therefore convex. Along a line through 0, its two slopes are -f(-e) and f(e), which are correctly ordered because f is positive away from 0. Hence f is globally convex.

Its unit sublevel is exactly the union (3). It is bounded and contains a disk about 0, since there are finitely many bounded sector pieces and f is continuous on the unit circle. Thus it is a convex body. All ray endpoints and sector areas have the required values, proving sufficiency.

## 4. Convexity of the feasibility system and an explicit compact domain

Each term a/u or a/(t-u), with a>=0 and t fixed, is convex on 0<u<t. Therefore the left sides of (2), after substituting v_i=t_i-u_i, are convex functions of the u variables. The right sides are fixed geometric data.

If a_i=0, changing u_i,v_i along u_i+v_i=1 has no effect on any constraint (2), and the geometric sector remains its core triangle. Fix u_i=v_i=1/2 in that case.

For a_i>0, the constraints at its two endpoint rays force

    kappa_i>0,  kappa_(i+1)>0,
    u_i>=L_i:=D_(i+1) a_i/kappa_(i+1),
    v_i>=R_i:=D_(i-1) a_i/kappa_i.               (6)

Thus u_i belongs to the explicit closed interval

    L_i<=u_i<=t_i-R_i.                           (7)

The interval must be nonempty. Its endpoints stay strictly inside (0,t_i), because L_i,R_i>0. Conversely, replacing the open domain by (7) loses no feasible point: (6) was a consequence of (2), and every point in (7) still has positive u_i,v_i. Require kappa_i>=0 for all i; if kappa_i=0, (2) forces both adjacent excesses a_(i-1),a_i to vanish. An index with positive excess and a nonpositive adjacent kappa is infeasible.

After these explicit preliminary checks, the feasible set is a closed convex subset of a finite compact box, and all its reciprocal expressions are continuous there. This proves compact attainment of feasibility, including all zero-excess and collinear-core cases.

## 5. Polynomial and charging forms

Clearing only the positive denominators in (2) yields the equivalent bilinear inequalities

    D_i a_(i-1)v_i+D_(i-1)a_i u_(i-1)
       <=kappa_i u_(i-1)v_i,                    (8)

together with u_i+v_i=t_i and the positive/compact-domain conditions above. Thus the finite system can also be used without rational-function divisions.

There is a useful additive normalization. Define

    b_i=kappa_i/[D_(i-1)D_i],
    h_i=a_i/(D_i t_i)=1/D_i-1/(2A_i).

For positive a_i put

    r_i=a_i/(D_i u_i),  s_i=a_i/(D_i v_i).

Then (2) and u_i+v_i=t_i are exactly

    r_(i-1)+s_i<=b_i,
    r_i s_i/(r_i+s_i)=h_i.                       (9)

For a_i=0 set r_i=s_i=h_i=0. This is only a reparametrization of the proved geometric feasibility system; no independent free allocation of cap masses is introduced.

The strict endpoint positivity and the compact formulation in Section 4 must be retained when using (8) or (9). Allowing an unconstrained zero denominator would admit a spurious point which extends one of the fixed ray endpoints.

## 6. An eliminated simultaneous-area inequality

Every feasible actual body satisfies the following relation involving all its sector areas at once:

    sum_i 1/A_i >= sum_i 1/D_i
                  +(1/2)sum_i E_i/[D_(i-1)D_i].              (10)

Indeed the nonnegative charge pairs in (9) satisfy r_i+s_i>=4h_i, because (r_i-s_i)^2>=0. Adding all vertex budgets therefore gives sum_i b_i>=4sum_i h_i. Substitution yields (10). Every A_i is positive since it is at least D_i/2>0. This is an exact necessary joint-area constraint, not an assertion that its single inequality is sufficient; the full six-variable system retains additional compatibility.

## 7. Supplementary exact checks

The shared verifier `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_fixed_endpoint_sector_polygon_replacement_slab_recovery.py` now passes **32,735 exact rational checks**. Besides reconstructing actual convex polygons with the required endpoints, supports, sector areas and cap areas, it verifies every reciprocal inequality, its exact identity with the corresponding vertex-turn determinant, all compact lower bounds, the charge identities, and (10). Core, bounded endpoint wedges, and an actual unbounded endpoint-wedge configuration are exercised. The theorem itself is proved without computational evidence.
